# @vllnt/convex-permissions

> Role-based access control (RBAC) component for Convex: runtime-editable roles, wildcard grants, scoped multi-tenant checks, and a typed TypeScript client.

A Convex component with two tables: `roles` (a role name and its grants) and `assignments` (an opaque `subjectRef`, a role, and an optional opaque `scopeRef`). The `Permissions<TRole, TAction>` client exposes `defineRole`, `removeRole`, `assign`, `revoke`, `check`, `require`, `rolesFor`, `permissionsFor`, and `listRoles`. Grants match exactly, by trailing `.*` prefix, or by `"*"`. Checks are default-deny; `require` throws a `ConvexError` with `data.code` `"FORBIDDEN"`. Peer `convex@^1.45.0`, Node.js `>=20`.

## For coding agents

These docs ship in `node_modules/@vllnt/convex-permissions/` and match the installed version: this file, `README.md`, `docs/API.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the TypeScript source in `src/`.

## When to use

- Use it when roles and grants must change at runtime without a redeploy.
- Use it when a subject holds different roles per tenant, org, or workspace (`scopeRef`).
- Use it when you need default-deny checks from Convex queries, mutations, actions, and HTTP actions, typed by your role and action unions.
- Do not use it for relationship-based access (ReBAC): model relationships in your own tables and indexes.
- Do not use it for attribute-based policies (ABAC): check resource fields in your own query or mutation code.
- Do not use it for roles fixed at deploy time: a typed `Record<Role, Action[]>` helper in your own code is enough.
